Roguelikes always incorporate an element of luck, but this is just ridiculous. Because you get dealt a hand randomly and your dice can repeat, you end up with many turns where you're unable to block or push damage when needed, or you're relying on curses to stun which is also unreliable, and because healing is scarce even if you make it out of a tough fight a little battered you're screwed against the area boss. Enemies have insane health pools by the end and it's way too random to hope you can construct the upgrades and corruptions that would let you form a real strategy. And even if you have say, a summon focused build, if you don't pull enough of your summon dice then you're just dead. I've played slot machine roguelikes with less randomness. Invoking Dicey Dungeons on the store page is a real joke, considering everything that game did to let you twist the rolls in your favor. Love the aesthetics, wish the game was better.
best in show for dogs that are also witches

[h3]巫师狗狗闯关录[/h3] 《Dog Witch》（汪!巫!录!）是一款肉鸽卡牌类的闯关游戏，游戏的主角是一只可以站立行走还会魔法的可爱狗狗。给狗狗取一个好听或者霸气的名字，选好身体各个部位的形状，找到喜欢的毛发颜色，还能调整它的体型和圆润程度，想要迷你狗也好，巨人狗也好，通通都能实现，最后修饰一下它的叫声，就可以开启闯关之路了。 进入闯关后，每个区域都有3个难度逐渐上升的普通战斗和一场艰难的BOSS战。在每回合开始时需要通过掷骰子来抽取5张卡牌进行战斗，卡牌的种类分为6种，法术书/魔杖/诅咒/法术/召唤物/骨头。 法术书可以给小狗的魔力充能，初始上限为3点，使用魔杖可以对敌人造成伤害，伤害点数和当前魔力值息息相关。法术根据当前持有的法术有不同的充能量，使用一次法术水晶获得1个充能点，充满之后才可以使用法术。召唤物是狗狗的好帮手，可以在左右各召唤一个，重复使用会提高召唤物的强度，骨头则会为狗狗提供抵挡伤害的护盾，诅咒有一定几率给敌人施加负面效果，在击败BOSS后可以对一件物品魔化来提供更加强力的效果。 在每一场战斗胜利后，都有战利品可以选择，战利品不仅可以改版并加强当前的卡牌效果，还可能会有强力的装备，装备分为戒指，手镯和项链，每一种都只能同时携带一件。除此之外还有一件特殊的装备——帽子。帽子可以看做是游戏内的局外成长元素，通过在关卡中完成条件获得，每个不同的帽子都有独特的效果。 帽子获取条件： 魔化：通关沙漠区域解锁。 时髦：死完三次后解锁。 大师：通关游戏解锁。 软糖：击败BOSS时生命值为1解锁。 无尽：佩戴大师帽子通过游戏解锁。 恶魔：装备恶魔手镯通过游戏解锁。 BOSS：通关游戏5次解锁。 宾基：装备宾基项链通关解锁。 虽然游戏有肉鸽元素存在，但是战斗过于依赖运气，因为抽卡需要通过掷骰子来进行，每一张牌都是随机生成的，即使有重新投掷的次数也无法保证可以抽到适于当前情况的卡牌，一旦运气不够好，连续多次抽到无法改变战况的牌就会战斗失利。在全随机的内容之下，本来构筑build就比较困难，通过抽卡的形式战斗随机性太高，艰难的构筑好build后也无法确保自己抽到好牌，让游戏的策略性变得偏低，而运气成为了影响成败的决定性因素。 [quote] 游玩百态，将游玩心得用汉语化作玩家的指明灯，(๑•̀ㅂ•́)و✧ [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/35402408/]点击这里关注汉化语录~[/url] 如果喜欢这个评测，请点个赞让更多人看见 [/quote]

[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/44181848/] 【更多适合Steam Deck的好游戏推荐，请关注GPD掌机鉴赏家！】[/url] 被严重低估的瑰宝《汪！巫！录！》值得更多国内玩家发现！超级好玩！ 魔法骰子与卡牌构筑的完美融合，却鲜为人知 作为一名热衷于肉鸽卡牌游戏的玩家，我在Steam上偶然发现了《汪！巫！录！》这款游戏，在体验后，我不得不承认这是近期最令我惊喜的独立游戏之一。然而令人遗憾的是，这样一款精品游戏在国内玩家中的知名度却低得可怜。 独特的游戏机制：骰子构筑的创新融合 《汪！巫！录！》巧妙地将骰子驱动的随机性与卡牌构筑的策略深度结合在一起。游戏中，你不再是从牌库中直接抽牌，而是通过投掷魔法骰子来决定可用的卡牌。这种设计既保留了肉鸽游戏固有的随机性，又增加了策略层面的思考维度。 与《杀戮尖塔》等传统卡牌构筑游戏不同，你需要考虑的不是单纯的卡牌组合，而是如何最大化利用每次骰子的结果。游戏中有150多种独特物品可供组合，每一次尝试都能发现新的协同效应和策略角度。 令人沉浸的游戏氛围 游戏的艺术风格独具匠心，迷幻的嘻哈音乐与异想天开的视觉效果相得益彰，营造出一种轻松愉快的氛围。你会发现自己不由自主地沉浸在狗狗巫师的魔法世界中，忘却现实生活的烦恼。 自定义系统也是游戏的一大亮点，你可以自由选择狗狗的毛发、帽子、叫声甚至体型，这种个性化设定大大增强了玩家与游戏角色之间的情感连接。 国内玩家缺失的遗憾 考虑到游戏的高质量，它在国内玩家中的低知名度令人困惑。可能的原因之一是独立游戏在Steam平台上面临的巨大竞争——每年有上万款游戏在Steam发行，使得优秀的小众作品难以脱颖而出。 结语：不应被埋没的精品 《汪！巫！录！》是一款将策略深度与轻松娱乐完美平衡的佳作。它提供了足够的挑战性满足核心玩家，同时又有可爱的画风和易上手的机制吸引休闲玩家。 如果你喜欢《杀戮尖塔》、《骰子地下城》这类游戏，或者单纯想体验一款独特而有趣的卡牌游戏，我强烈推荐你尝试《汪！巫！录！》。它不仅值得你的时间和金钱，更值得被更多国内玩家发现和欣赏。 希望未来能在游戏的中文社区看到更多关于这款游戏的讨论，让这颗被埋没的宝石能够闪耀它应有的光芒。

Aesthetically very creative and pleasing. Gameplay is very disappointing. I think the largest drawback is the lack of options to manipulate dice odds. Sure there is the three-reroll mechanic that is in place so that builds aren't completely unviable, but even then, creating a scaling build doesn't seem satsifying because there's simply too little player ability to ensure or increase the odds that the right dice are rolled. A build that scales on bones and summons can be ruined by a bad roll. A build that scales on wand damage can be ruined by a bad roll. A build that scales on mana can be ruined by a bad roll. Usually roguelikes offset bad rng by either adding player skill into the mix (i.e. Binding of Isaac) or adding odds-manipulation (i.e. Dicey Dungeons, or any deckbuilder), but here that key feature simply isn't implemented far enough. For the current state of the game, it feels like slot machine that lets you pick which fruit should count as a 7, but with no way of rigging the machine. I'd wait for the devs to hopefully add more along these lines before buying.

I first played the Demo back in Spring, and was also a beta tester. I like Dog Witch, and I want to love it, but I cannot truly recommend it. Gameplay results are ultimately dictated by RNG, not skill. When I lose, I mostly think "I wish I had gotten better dice", not "Oooohh, that mistake is why I lost." A great example of this reliance on RNG hurting the game is the mechanic where enemies sometimes try to steal your dice. The only way of stopping this is to stun the enemy, and you can (sometimes, depending on other RNG) try to prepare for this by preemptively lowering the enemy's curse resist. But even if this works, the enemy will (somewhat randomly, it seems) try to steal your dice on the next turn as well, once they're back at full curse resist! This leads to frustration and ultimately failure as one of your dice gets stolen, you lose momentum, and can't try to prepare for the next time a die will be stolen. Ultimately, the game needs some additional mechanics that let you manipulate the odds of getting certain dice rolls over others. Barring that, some additional ways to adjust difficult: for example, giving you options to increase how much health or dice you start with. With some additional mechanics to temper RNG, this game would be truly great. I love the theming and the music, and I love that I can start a run and finish in 15-20 minutes. But more often than not, I leave the game feeling frustrated and like I can't truly influence the outcome of the game.

有点不太理解为啥中译名要是汪!巫!录!，还要在名字中间加符号，这非常影响游戏的搜索，而且本身英文名非常直白，DOG WITCH，狗巫师，言简意赅，直抒胸臆。 原本以为又是一个萌狗+卡牌的普通肉鸽游戏，上手玩了几把虽然连第一张图都没打过就挂了，但意外的还挺有意思，主要还是得益于简洁卡牌内容。游戏每局开始，点选骰子，会根据骰子点数从六件装备中随机选择，分别是法术书、魔杖、诅咒、法术、召唤物、骨头，骰子的点数是看不到的，只能根据生成出的装备来进行判断。其中法术书使用后可以为魔杖充能，吃2本书后魔杖的效果将发挥到最大；魔杖就是主要攻击手段，所能造成的伤害值受法术点数影响；诅咒是可以对地方进行debuff的施加进行控制的手段；法术的施展需要先攒满该法术所对应的法术值，跟魔杖不同初始就有1点可以发动进攻，法术值不满是无法施展法术的；召唤物就是临时的帮手，具有血量和攻击力，在己方出手时发起进攻，也会吸引敌方的攻击；骨头就是临时护盾，当前回合有效，是有效的保命手段。除此以外，还有戒指、手镯、项链，再对魔杖、法术、诅咒、召唤物的效果进行额外效果添加，使其更为强力。再完成了一个章节的Boss挑战后，还将解锁装备的魔化效果，魔化效果相当强力，但也有副作用会扣除一定数量的生命值，为了获得魔化效果，需要进行取舍。 在装备种类不齐的情况下，还是挺难通关的，血量默认13点非常少了，要是没有有效的防护手段是很难走到后期的。不过帽子叠加可以获得诸如魔化装备不再扣除血量，非常好用，也是在帽子叠加后才碰巧通关了。游戏的卡牌数量不算多，所能组的卡组效果也不多，游玩时保护自己存活下来远比进攻更为重要，那就需要尽可能多的保命手段，直接回血的卡牌效果并不多，大多都是需要满足相应的条件方能生效，当敌人怎么打都打不死，血还越打越多的时，那是真挺爽的，哪怕把我限制到生命只有5，都很难死了。 总的来说，狗巫师的难度不大，卡组也少，骰子与卡牌的结合，算不上新颖，但也做出了自己的特色，有限装备的变化限制了策略的深度，作为一款休闲肉鸽卡牌小品，可能玩不到太久的时间就玩透了。 [quote]关注[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/36224058/]老实人鉴赏家 [/url] [url=https://steamcommunity.com/groups/laoshirenLSR]老实人评测[/url]：独立游戏爱好者聚集地，黄油绅士交流中心。 不错过游戏的亮点，不放过游戏的槽点，带给玩家最直观的测评感受。[/quote]

There's the bones (no pun intended) of something really fun here - the general vibes are great, the art style is fun, the music is a bop. But sadly each run is too punishingly random to be enjoyable, with too few tools to mitigate it or recover from bad streaks - It feels like no matter how you play, you're always only one or two bad turns away from failing an entire run for reasons completely outside your control (you might not roll shields, your stuns might not work, and most enemies pick random targets by default so you can't even reliably mitigate damage with summons). Couple that with a lack of a tutorial or any real explanation of key mechanics outside of mouse-over keywords, and most runs just feel frustrating. I'll probably still stubbornly plug away until I get *a* clear, but can't recommend this game until its had a balance pass or two at least.

[h3] Not recommended. [/h3] This feels like an [b] early access [/b] game but doesn't have the label. Either wait for updates or [b] spend your money on a better game [/b] in the same genre. Beyond the gameplay there's a bunch of missing quality of life features that make playing it fun for longer sessions. The biggest example is no replay button after losing a run. It boots you out to the menu and you have to navigate back to the same difficulty you were on- wasting a bunch of time. Bugs are common- like steam achievements not being implemented, etc. Gameplay itself is ok until you put a few hours in to it then realize how lackluster it becomes. Most of the difficulty is fighting the game itself instead of the enemies it presents you. You can't really have any plan of attack or think of good synergistic builds because it's entirely way too random. The biggest glaring issues I see is that you can't manipulate your luck and items become useless when you roll something that's already at maximum capacity. So a lot of the time you have a bunch of useless duds that do nothing. I think even if all the issues are fixed the enemy design and player items are really bland. [h3] The game doesn't offer anything cool and unique. [/h3]

As it stands i cant recommend this game on gameplay alone. maybe for the price its a good time waster for a couple hours but thats kind of it. The problem for me is, I feel the game completely hinges on sustainability through these mini gauntlets. the only real way to sustain is to get bones for shielding. If you get unlucky and roll no bones, well that's it, and very few items can heal if you even get them on and not very efficiently. as other reviewers might have pointed out, there is no control or influence over dice rolls to help apply the build you are going for and as simple as the game is i dont think there is even room for such a change.

EDIT: Played another 2 hours and still a BS final boss that's damn near impossible to beat. Steal all your die, spawn bosses, spawn minions and you can't do sh1t about it Took me until over the refund window to actually make it to the RNGesus Wizard, who I managed to get down to 50HP after he'd spawned 3 lots of 2 bosses After many, MANY, runs of dying over and over because I couldn't roll any defence or get any heals you finally get to the final boss, who just spawns the previous bosses every couple of turns, meaning you have to get stupidly lucky to win It genuinely feels like there is no skill involved and it's just a pure luck game. No matter what build you go with, you just have to repeat over and over until you get that 1-in-a-1000 God run to finally beat the end boss, which I just don't think I have the patience to do Luckily the game is cheap, otherwise I'd be so annoyed. It's getting really tiresome where games just think we want crappy RNG over skill Also, not sure how it can be considered a "deck-builder" when you're limited to 5 dice and 3 "relics(?)". If there was the option to have more than 1 summon/book/spell/bone it could probably make the game more bearable, but I doubt it Might come back to it if there are some balance patches in the future

It's the same vibe as a free flash game. Very short, briefly interesting concept, cute graphics, neat soundtrack. Would I pay $10 for a flash game with a 1~ hour gameplay loop again? Probably not. $2, maybe. The gameplay is frustrating. It's a strategy game, but entirely luck based. Playing well, strategically, is far too unlikely to win you a run. There are far too many opportunities for bad luck to ruin a run.

as a huge fan of dicey dungeons, games like slay the spire don't really capture my attention; the dice are what really make it fun for me. for a long time i've been looking for something that scratches a similar itch. nothing else has really done it for me until dog witch. the dice add the perfect amount of randomness without having to read and learn tons of different card effects and getting bogged down in lots of math. everything is simple to understand but there is still plenty of depth. there are so many items which can have interesting interactions with each other, and the hats (which can be mixed and matched) add an additional layer of variety and challenge. i also really love the art direction and style. it's cute and silly, with all kinds of strange creatures that somehow all work together in the world being presented. the music is nice and relaxing, too. it helps that i am both a dog and a witch irl, so i can deeply relate to the main character. being called a "bad dog" makes me crave vengeance! i am NOT a bad dog!!

If you like RNG The Game™ then this game will be for you. Allies attack randomly, enemies (for the most part) attack randomly, status effects are applied with % chance (which can make or break combat) and are fleeting, items are rolled randomly with no rerolls, the things you are able to do on a turn are rolled randomly. If you throw yourself at this game for long enough then the odds will be in your favour, but for the most part you're going to get saddled with garbage spells, items, and abilities that are bizarrely balanced, that don't synergise or work very well, and will cause you to lose by the second level. The aesthetics of this game are fantastic and cute, and there's a lot of potential for the game to be more, but it still needs some work.

Dog Witch is a quirky and enjoyable casual roguelite. Not too much to the deckbuilding here - there are a few nifty synergies here and there, but mostly, good tactical play will get you through to the end regardless of your build. Simple enough for my 5 year old to get through most of a run, which accounts for a fair amount of my playtime :) Overall, would be a reasonable buy at the price. I don't recommend it because of the bugs. A recent patch outright broke leveling up. That got rolled back, but I've encountered frequent and diverse new bugs since then. Many effects don't apply when they are supposed to (for example: the Master Hat's enemy buff seems to not work now until you restart the game), or have a broken lifecycle in some other way - for example, the debuff to your reroll count from a certain necklace will carry over into a new game. Sometimes the enemy simply doesn't start their turn and the fight has to be restarted. On mac, the game goes into windowed mode when going to the title screen, but I consider this only an inconvenience. Dog Witch's bugs are frequent enough to cause frustration. I hope to change this to a positive review soon when I see some fixes.

It's a fun game. Lotta RNG. Different starts. I do recommend it. Only thing I don't like is that it doesn't save your video savings. Every restart brings it back to 1280. Good for $10. You can pet the dog.

It's a cute game with a simple premise ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ is it a game for lucky people. I've had runs where I've rolled 0 bones in 6 rerolls over 2 rounds, I've had rounds where someone swings all 3 times on me with two minions three times in a row, everything feels insanely punishing and rerolling 3 times for 2 out of the 6 items you still coming up short feels like it's happening more often than not. It feels unbalanced in the sense that no matter what I do, it's impossible to optimise the luck aspect. It feels bad to play more often than not, it feels insanely punishing constantly. Enemies scale and take away your wand chargers (therefore damage) each time they hit you, gems are all but useless 99% of the time because if you scale it up at no immediate benefit, and then you'll roll 1 charged item when you activate it and waste all rerolls and land on 4 useless items. It's a fight between taking damage to get in early shots, or turtling and having nothing to show for it. You can get lucky with items, some are very good, but I've not had a single ounce of luck with gem runs or monster runs, as often they take longer to warm up than wand builds and by that point most creatures are hitting you for 5 damage a go and you can't just shield it away. Making a build works up until you go against enemies that are unfavourable to it. Diversifying means you have your fingers in too many pies and it doesn't work, and often you have incompatible items that have no synergy because you have a choice of 3 with no rerolls. If you want cute dogs and games of chance this is for you. Unfortunately this is not remotely a skill based game, and consistently runs on the unlucky side in my experience

DOG WITCH is a roguelike deckbuilding game that takes a ridiculous premise and transforms it into an unexpectedly clever and highly addictive strategy experience. Developed by Heckmouse and published by Mystic Forge, the game follows a magical dog battling bizarre enemies and dangerous bosses using enchanted dice, wands, summons, and strange magical artifacts. At first glance, the colorful visuals and absurd humor make the game look like a lightweight comedy project, but underneath the goofy presentation is a surprisingly well-designed roguelike filled with meaningful tactical choices, satisfying build experimentation, and fast-paced combat that constantly encourages “just one more run.” The gameplay revolves around turn-based encounters powered by dice rolls and randomized abilities. Each turn, players roll magical dice that determine what actions can be performed, including attacks, defensive spells, summons, shield generation, status effects, and wand abilities. The dice mechanics create a constant balance between luck and strategy because players must decide whether to keep their current rolls or reroll in hopes of creating stronger combinations. Unlike some roguelikes that overwhelm players with endless layers of complicated systems, DOG WITCH keeps its mechanics straightforward and easy to understand while still offering enough depth to support creative and powerful builds. One of the game’s greatest strengths is how satisfying its build variety becomes over time. Every run introduces new relics, magical items, cursed equipment, summons, and wand upgrades capable of completely changing how combat plays out. Some builds revolve around overwhelming enemies with summoned allies, while others focus on stacking defensive shields, abusing status effects, or creating devastating burst-damage combinations through powerful wand synergies. The game constantly rewards experimentation because even seemingly weak items can become extremely powerful when combined with the right abilities and modifiers. The item system plays a huge role in maintaining replayability. With a large pool of magical artifacts and corrupted equipment available, no two runs feel exactly the same. Corrupted items are especially interesting because they provide major advantages while introducing dangerous drawbacks that force players to adapt their strategy. Some cursed relics create high-risk, high-reward builds capable of becoming absurdly overpowered if managed correctly. Discovering unexpected synergies between items becomes one of the game’s most enjoyable aspects because successful runs often evolve in unpredictable ways. Combat pacing is another area where DOG WITCH succeeds remarkably well. Battles are quick, responsive, and easy to restart after failure, which keeps momentum high throughout long sessions. The game wastes very little time between encounters, allowing players to focus almost entirely on strategic decision-making and build progression. Runs generally remain compact enough to finish in shorter play sessions, making the game ideal for quick bursts of gameplay without sacrificing the rewarding progression systems that define strong roguelikes. The reroll mechanics also help reduce frustration caused by bad luck. While randomness is still a major part of the experience, players usually have opportunities to salvage poor turns through smart resource management and reroll decisions. This system creates a more engaging form of randomness where players are constantly adapting rather than simply accepting defeat because of unlucky outcomes. Managing limited rerolls becomes an important tactical layer on its own, especially during difficult boss fights. Visually, DOG WITCH embraces a deliberately silly and chaotic art style that gives the game a huge amount of personality. The colorful environments, cartoon enemies, and exaggerated animations reinforce the game’s absurd sense of humor without interfering with gameplay readability. Enemy designs are especially memorable, ranging from strange magical creatures and aggressive insects to bizarre fantasy machines and heavily armed nesting dolls. The game fully commits to its weird atmosphere, and that commitment helps it stand out strongly from more generic fantasy roguelikes. The soundtrack contributes heavily to the overall charm as well. Relaxed lo-fi-inspired music blends surprisingly well with the frantic tactical gameplay, creating a tone that feels cozy and energetic at the same time. The sound effects are playful and satisfying, giving attacks, spells, and summons enough impact without overwhelming the experience. Combined with the game’s humor and visual style, the audio design helps maintain a consistently enjoyable atmosphere even during repeated runs. Another enjoyable feature is the cosmetic customization system. Players can unlock hats, visual upgrades, and modifiers that not only personalize the Dog Witch but sometimes alter gameplay conditions as well. These additions help reinforce the game’s playful personality while giving experienced players additional ways to challenge themselves through modified runs and alternate strategies. However, DOG WITCH is not completely without flaws. Randomness can occasionally become frustrating despite the reroll systems designed to soften bad luck. Some runs still depend heavily on favorable item drops or strong dice outcomes, especially during difficult boss encounters where poor rolls can quickly destroy an otherwise promising build. While strategy and adaptation remain important, there are moments where the game leans too heavily on RNG. The game’s relatively compact structure may also reduce long-term appeal for some players. Although the build variety creates strong replayability, experienced players will eventually begin recognizing familiar enemy patterns, dominant strategies, and recurring item combinations. Compared to larger roguelike deckbuilders with massive content pools and extensive progression systems, DOG WITCH feels somewhat smaller in scale. It remains highly entertaining, but it is probably best enjoyed in shorter sessions rather than endless marathon playthroughs. The simplistic visual style may also divide players. The intentionally rough and exaggerated presentation lacks the technical polish of larger roguelikes, and some players may initially dismiss the game because of its childish appearance. However, the humor, creativity, and strong gameplay systems behind the visuals help compensate for the lack of graphical sophistication. Despite these issues, DOG WITCH succeeds because its core gameplay loop is consistently fun and rewarding. The combination of dice-based combat, fast-paced progression, bizarre humor, and highly flexible build experimentation creates an experience that feels approachable while still offering meaningful strategic depth. The game understands how to make roguelike progression addictive without burying players under unnecessary complexity. For fans of deckbuilders, dice-based strategy games, and roguelikes built around experimentation and replayability, DOG WITCH delivers a charming and highly entertaining experience filled with creative item combinations and memorable encounters. It may not rival the largest games in the genre in terms of content volume, but its personality, clever mechanics, and satisfying combat systems make it one of the more enjoyable indie roguelikes available. Rating: 8/10

This game is borkin' wild and I love it! As a big card gamer, I was really happy to see they added the Vampire mode, which turns the game from a dicebuilder into a deckbuilder! WELL TOO BAD BECAUSE OOPS ALL BEES, BAYBEE!!! C:<). Aesthetically, this game is also just amazing. The models are really adorable/weird, there's an interesting variety of enemy/summon concepts and most importantly, you can customize your doggo, bork with it AND pet it too! In addition, the music is such a vibe; it's quite chill and got some nice beats to it. Overall, I've had such a fantastic time with it so far with these quick runs and I can easily see myself coming back for more, especially since the dev is actively updating the game pretty frequently! Thank you so much to Heckmouse and the rest of the team for such a wacky, fun game and for making me Laff all night with a capital L and two Fs.
